clue.text: Joy to find food shop by good hotel on the square

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared food
G is the standard abbreviation for good
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a T-square is the draughtsman's ruler, so square can give T

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to discover a delicatessen next to a fine hotel on the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit side by side in clue order: DELI, G, H, T. 'By' and 'on' only place them next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight is a straightforward synonym for joy, a feeling of great pleasure.

clue.text: "Darling" — that is a term of endearment

parts.note: dear is a word for a darling
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A note explaining that calling someone darling is an affectionate expression.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a dictionary entry, but 'that is' supplies its own abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearie is an affectionate form of address, used like love or pet to someone liked.

clue.text: Symbol's very powerful, shut down

parts.note: a logo is a symbol representing a company
ff is fortissimo in music, meaning very loud or powerful

explanation.surface: A mighty emblem has been closed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very powerful' is the musical marking ff, fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: To log off is to end a computer session, closing one's access the way one shuts down a machine.

clue.text: Manifestations of fear when silly fool knocks

parts.note: calling someone a silly goose means they are a fool
bumps are knocks

explanation.surface: People show fright when an idiot comes banging at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Goosebumps are the pimpled skin raised by cold or fright, a visible sign of being scared.

clue.text: Two hotels in rural district originally winning bronze award?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a description: the award for coming third

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only each word's opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Two country hotels share a prize at a local competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotels and district look like NATO H and RD abbreviations, but 'originally' takes the first letter of all five words.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronze medal goes to whoever finishes in third place, so the bronze award stands for third.

clue.text: Extremely excited after gown was prepared

indicators.note: after says the second chunk comes behind the first in the answer, fixing the order of the parts

parts.note: a gown is a dress
the extreme letters, first and last, of excited

explanation.surface: Someone was thrilled to bits once the gown was ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' points at the two end letters of excited, which go after the gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is dressed, like a salad or crab, has been prepared for the table, so the past tense works as a synonym.

clue.text: Oh dear, air's polluted, causing illness

indicators.note: polluted means spoilt and messed up, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone laments that dirty air is making people sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The British spelling with -OE- is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Diarrhoea is an upset of the bowels, a common illness or symptom of one.

clue.text: Trendsetting makes one nervous

definitions.meaning: first meaning: daringly fashionable and avant-garde
second meaning: tense and on edge

explanation.surface: Being at the cutting edge of fashion gives one the jitters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fashionably provocative and anxious or irritable, two quite separate senses.

clue.text: Edward, second lock forward, is under pressure

indicators.note: forward says the following chunks are placed in front, ahead of the first one named

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a lock of hair is a tress
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A rugby player called Edward, playing as a second-row lock forward, is feeling the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a lock forward plays in the second row, which disguises the pieces; here 'forward' sends second and lock ahead of Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stressed means feeling strain and anxiety, the state of being under pressure.

clue.text: Painstaking policeman, liberal, a fine fellow

parts.note: a DI is a Detective Inspector
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
a means one, and I is the Roman numeral for one
a gent is a gentleman, a fine fellow

explanation.surface: A meticulous police officer, open-minded and a thoroughly decent chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone diligent takes great care and effort over work, which is what painstaking describes.

clue.text: One child's horse runs round causing annoyance

parts.note: one can be the article a
a gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A child's pony bolts round the paddock and causes a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs round' looks like the horse's action, but it is two pieces: R for runs and O for something round. Aggro is British slang for aggravation or trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British slang for aggravation, so it means trouble or annoyance.

clue.text: Gun Laura and I rigged for the opening stage

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: something rigged has been tampered with and rearranged, so the letters are set up afresh

parts.note: the letters of these three words, without the and

explanation.surface: Laura and the speaker fix up a starting pistol for the first leg of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' just joins Laura and I; its letters are not used.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event or speech is the first one, marking the beginning of something.

clue.text: Fashionable cricketers play baseball too!

definitions.note: a cryptic hint describing the answer as players, not a direct synonym

parts.note: what is in is fashionable
the players of the side not batting in cricket

explanation.surface: Trendy cricketers turn out for a game of baseball as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: infielders are both a type of cricket fielder and the players at first, second, third and shortstop in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the infielders are the four players stationed around the bases, so they do play baseball.

clue.text: Decline some invitations again

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of invitations and the start of again

explanation.surface: Turn down a few invitations a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: Decline looks like refusing the invitations, but it is the definition in its sense of sinking or drooping.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to sink or droop, and a decline is a drop, as in prices sagging.

clue.text: It's apparent that there is nothing sensible about time

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word before it wraps around what follows

parts.note: taken as written
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A remark that obviously there's no common sense in someone's timekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing sensible' reads as a complaint, but nothing is O, and sensible goes round time after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means seeming or professed, what appears on the surface, so it is close to apparent.

clue.text: Vessel with a comic quality?

parts.note: surface reading: a blood vessel that is somehow funny
setter's reading: a streak of wit in someone's writing or manner, described with the word for a blood vessel

explanation.walkthrough: A vein is both a blood vessel and a streak or strain of character, so a vein of humour reads literally as a joking blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous vein is a strain of comedy running through a person's talk or writing, a comic quality.

clue.text: Freshly made cocoa's in supply initially at such events

indicators.note: something freshly made has been put together anew, so the letters are newly arranged

parts.note: the letters of these words

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of that word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of supply

explanation.surface: Hot chocolate is made up fresh and on hand at certain functions.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasions are particular events or happenings, especially special social ones.

clue.text: Rustic yarn?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: simple, plain and unsophisticated

definitions.note: homespun is also the noun for cloth or yarn spun at home
definitions.meaning: second meaning: thread spun at home by hand

explanation.walkthrough: Yarn tempts as a tall tale, but here it is thread; the question mark marks the play on that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both plain country simplicity and fabric or thread spun at home by hand.

clue.text: String up and fix the mainstay

parts.note: to lynch is to hang someone without trial
to pin something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: Hang and fasten the key support.
explanation.definitionFit: A lynchpin is the pin holding a wheel on its axle, hence the central person or thing everything depends on.

clue.text: Swinging calypso gem I'm giving this international event …

indicators.note: swinging suggests moving to and fro, so the letters are swung into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A singer boasts that their lively calypso hit is fit for a global festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, which uses the same event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympic Games are the world's leading international multi-sport event, held every four years.

clue.text: Swelling love Medea's disposed to exhibit

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: disposed means set out or arranged, so the letters are placed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Medea, the vengeful heroine of Greek myth, is inclined to show her love.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedema is the medical term for swelling caused by fluid collecting in body tissue.

clue.text: Road to this Somerset village

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a public road in a town
second meaning: a large village in Somerset, a county in south-west England, home of Clarks shoes

explanation.surface: A signpost points the way to a little village in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road lined with buildings, and Street is also the proper name of a Somerset village.

clue.text: … where each training course initially is for the others

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of each word is used

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Continuing the Olympic scene: wherever each training course begins, it is meant for the rest of the athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue only for the surface; the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc abbreviates et cetera, Latin for and the rest, so it stands for the others in a list.

clue.text: Amount to be paid to measure fellows' model

parts.note: to assess is to measure or evaluate
fellows are men
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model can give T

explanation.surface: A sum is charged for sizing up some chaps' design.
explanation.walkthrough: Model T is a crossword staple from Ford's early car.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a sum levied or charged, such as a tax or fee calculated for someone to pay.

clue.text: Merge together when English lied badly

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stories run together when an English speaker tells clumsy fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to run sounds or ideas into one, omitting a part, so things merge.

clue.text: Evil old hill in the north

definitions.note: an archaic adjective, as old signals
definitions.meaning: first meaning: cruel or deadly, an old-fashioned sense
second meaning: a hill or moor in northern England, as in the Lake District

explanation.surface: A sinister ancient hill somewhere in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is an archaic word for fierce or wicked, and also the name for an upland hill in Cumbria.

clue.text: Spice on one pizza topping

parts.note: pepper is a spice
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sprinkles seasoning over a single pizza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On one' reads as placing spice on a pizza, but both words are pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy dried sausage, sliced and very commonly put on pizzas.

clue.text: Be around clergyman to produce a musical note

indicators.note: around says the first word goes on either side of the second, wrapping it

parts.note: taken as written
Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: Stand near a vicar while he sings a long note.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note, equal to two semibreves, now rarely used.

clue.text: No awful little puns in puzzle!

indicators.note: awful means badly done, so the letters are mangled into another order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for little
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver complains that this crossword contains no dreadful little wordplay jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Puzzle is the definition as a verb, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to baffle or perplex them, so it means to puzzle.

clue.text: A gentle transformation that is chic

indicators.note: a transformation changes the form of something, so the letters are recast

parts.note: the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A soft makeover leaves someone looking stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant and chic are both words for being stylish and refined in appearance.
